lines.text: Yank your seatbelt, and it locks. Pull it slowly, and it doesn't. So how does it know?
Inside, the belt winds around a spool, with a ring of teeth on the side.
Lock one watches the car. A little pendulum hangs inside.
Brake hard, and it swings forward, and pushes a hook into the teeth.
Lock two watches the belt. Yank it, and the spool spins fast...
so a weighted lever swings outward, and locks the spool too.
That's the trick... two locks. Either one can hold you.
In the front seat, a belt cuts your risk of dying in a crash by forty-five percent.
So when it locks on you? It's doing its job.
